answer: In PoA, identity admission is tied to a Wesolowski VDF: producing the time-lock output requires a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result depending on the previous one, while the proof enables efficient verification. Creating many clones therefore cannot parallelize this work across GPUs; every identity consumes physical sequential time, limiting Sybil throughput. Neither an inlet nor a fable about a shortcut, nor any graph vertex, removes that bottleneck.
